intent: Adjudicate historical generic-api-key false positives for the exact public cryptography type identifier `Ed25519PrivateKey` with one rule-scoped, anchored exception; mechanically reject prefix, suffix, and case variants and forbid path-wide or commit-wide suppression while preserving full-history secret scanning.

negative_controls.name: broadened-ed25519-type-regex-is-rejected
negative_controls.command: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; import subprocess,sys; p=Path('.gitleaks.toml'); t=p.read_text(); old='^Ed25519PrivateKey$'; new='.*Ed25519PrivateKey.*'; assert old in t; p.write_text(t.replace(old,new,1)); r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pytest','-q','tests/test_gitleaks_config.py::test_ed25519_type_exception_is_exact_unique_and_rule_scoped'],check=False); p.write_text(t); sys.exit(0 if r.returncode!=0 else 1)"

interface_mismatches: The default generic-api-key heuristic treats a public cryptography class name as secret-shaped historical content even though a class identifier carries no credential authority.
A repository-global regex, file path, or commit allowlist would suppress unrelated findings; the exception therefore belongs only to the generic-api-key rule and matches only the anchored identifier.
honest_blockers: An allowlist exception is not proof that no secret exists; the contract proves only the syntactic scope of this one exception.
A local redacted full-history scan proves the accepted checkout and locally available history only; independent CI must repeat the scan against the final integrated commit before merge.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the exact rule-scoped regex, focused contract tests, and this packet together. Historical public-type false positives will again block full-history scanning; no history or scan result is altered by rollback.
